Lung Cancer.Smoking: Smoking is the leading cause of lung cancer, accounting for about 80% of cases.
Lung Cancer.Occupational Hazards: Exposure to asbestos, radon, and other carcinogens increases lung cancer risk.
Lung Cancer.Chest Pain: Persistent chest pain may indicate lung involvement.
Lung Cancer.Coughing of Blood: Hemoptysis is a serious symptom that requires immediate evaluation.

Breast Cancer.Obesity: Higher body fat increases estrogen levels, which may raise breast cancer risk.
Breast Cancer.Alcohol use: Regular alcohol consumption is linked to increased breast cancer risk.
Breast Cancer.Fatigue: Unexplained fatigue can be an early sign of various cancers.

Colorectal Cancer.Balanced Diet: Low-fiber, high-fat diets increase colorectal cancer risk.
Colorectal Cancer.Obesity: Excess weight increases inflammation and insulin resistance, raising cancer risk.
Colorectal Cancer.Fatigue: Persistent fatigue may be a sign of anemia from undetected bleeding.

Prostate Cancer.Genetic Risk: Men with a family history have a higher risk of developing prostate cancer.
Prostate Cancer.Obesity: Obesity is associated with more aggressive prostate cancer.

Skin Cancer.Occupational Hazards: Sun exposure and radiation are major risk factors for skin cancer.
Skin Cancer.Genetic Risk: Fair skin and family history increase skin cancer risk.
